name: Specluative Storytelling
description:
Speculative storytelling uses narrative to explore possible situations, futures and consequences through characters and events. Stories allow designers to examine how broad changes might be experienced in everyday life and to connect technological or systemic propositions with social relationships and values.

The aim is not prediction but structured imagination.
whenToUse: Use speculative storytelling when future conditions are too abstract to discuss productively or when a project needs to explore multiple perspectives on possible change.
steps: Identify the issue or change being explored.
Define the conditions that differ from the present.
Create characters with different relationships to those conditions.
Develop an everyday situation through which the future becomes visible.
Use the narratives to identify assumptions, questions and design implications.
lookOutFor: Avoid treating one story as *the* future.
Characters should not exist merely as devices for explaining technology.
Consider who benefits, who carries risk and whose perspective remains absent.

resources.citation: Candy, S. (2010). *The Futures of Everyday Life*. University of Hawai'i at Mānoa.
Dunne, A. & Raby, F. (2013). *Speculative Everything*. MIT Press.
